entries.title: Are you choosing to stay single? We want to hear from you

entries.title: Alien Terrorist Removal Court holds its first-ever hearing after 30 years
entries.snippet: Congress created the Alien Terrorist Removal Court in 1996 to make it easier for the Justice Department to use classified evidence to deport people from U.S. soil.

entries.title: Hope dwindles for rescue after southwestern Japan earthquake as death toll climbs to 25
entries.snippet: Time was running out to find survivors, as rescuers continued to work in the Kumamoto area on Japan's southern main island of Kyushu, where the magnitude 7.1 earthquake hit Tuesday. The number of people missing was unclear.

entries.snippet: Spain will deploy its military to restore order at its border with Morocco in Ceuta after thousands of migrants streamed into the tiny Spanish territory, with at least nine dying in the attempt.

entries.snippet: The long-running conflict in eastern Congo has driven nearly 10 million people into crisis or emergency levels of hunger, with Ituri — the epicenter of the Ebola outbreak — among the most affected with 1.9 million in need of food, according to the World Food Program.

entries.title: How views on Trump's handling of Iran have shifted, according to this poll

entries.title: Are Iran and Ukraine wars getting tangled in Caspian Sea?
entries.snippet: Tehran has threatened a response after a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea that Kyiv says was carrying weapons to Russia. Still, Ukraine says it wants to avoid escalation with Tehran.

entries.title: Spain will send troops to Ceuta to help with border security
entries.snippet: Authorities in the Spanish city of Ceuta asked Madrid to declare a national emergency and send military assistance. Crowds of people breached the border of the territory next to Morocco as police lost control.

entries.title: Kenya: 15 dead elephants likely poisoned by cyanide
entries.snippet: The elephants ate contaminated tomatoes from nearby farms. It was unclear if the poisoning was deliberate or accidental.

entries.title: Berlin Pride attack: Are German juvenile courts too lenient?
entries.snippet: The Islamist terror attack on Berlin Pride has put the work of juvenile courts into the spotlight. Many argue the 21-year-old perpetrator should have been in prison at the time of the attack.

entries.title: Epstein files: How victims remain exposed to identification
entries.snippet: US officials vowed to revise redactions after files exposed information that identified survivors of sexual abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and his associates. A DW investigation found that sensitive information remains online.

entries.title: UEFA votes to boycott World Cup over FIFA investor plan
entries.snippet: UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott ‌the ⁠World ⁠Cup and other competitions unless FIFA abandons its private investor plans. "The World Cup is not for sale," they said, as FIFA seeks to sell a stake in it.

entries.title: EU aims to build AI gigafactories of its own
entries.snippet: The EU has unveiled a plan to raise state and private funds to hyperscale AI capabilities and gain independence from non-European governments. The plan calls for the construction of seven new sites across the bloc.

entries.title: Human trafficking in Mexico: the dark side of tourism
entries.snippet: By May, a record-breaking 20 million tourists had visited Mexico so far in 2026. But with increased tourism comes a heightened risk of human trafficking and sexual exploitation. Women and children are most vulnerable.

entries.title: How crypto miners are stealing power in Southeast Asia
entries.snippet: Across Southeast Asia, illegal cryptocurrency miners are stealing vast amounts of electricity, straining national grids and exposing links to organized crime.

entries.title: BMW to Volkswagen: How deep is Germany's auto industry cull?
entries.snippet: BMW joins VW, Porsche and Mercedes-Benz in cutting thousands of jobs, as Chinese rivals erode their market share. DW recaps the major reforms German automakers are pursuing to safeguard their future.

entries.title: Eurozone sees GDP growth of 0.4%, most since early 2025
entries.snippet: Eurozone economies expanded by 0.4% in the second quarter of 2026, exceeding expectations and marking the strongest quarterly growth since early 2025.

entries.title: Germany's heat death toll nears 10,000
entries.snippet: Germany's heat-related death toll for 2026 has already surpassed every full-year total since 2016 — and is expected to climb as another spell of extreme temperatures takes hold.

entries.title: Germany widens deportations to Afghanistan
entries.snippet: For the first time, Germany has deported a man with no criminal record to Kabul. Faridoon Tofan, who is currently in deportation detention, fears the same fate.

entries.title: Why Germany may stand up against FIFA's World Cup sell off
entries.snippet: Leading figures in German football have lined up to criticize Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell a stake in the World Cup. Germany is showing signs that they may ready to oppose Infantino's re-election.

entries.title: Poland says Russian ballistic missile violated airspace
entries.snippet: Polish authorities have said that a Russian ballistic missile crashed within its borders during Moscow's overnight attacks on Ukraine. No injuries were reported as Kyiv warned air defense in the region needs boosting.

entries.title: Danube water levels: Hungary, Romania cut nuclear output
entries.snippet: Historically low water levels along Europe's second-longest river have led Hungary and Romania to reduce output at key nuclear plants. Danube tourism and river cargo have also been severely affected by Europe's heatwave.

entries.title: Crete wildfires cause evacuations and firefighter deaths
entries.snippet: Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete are forcing thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate. Three firefighters have died as Greece becomes the latest country, after France and Spain, to face summer blazes.

entries.title: Deaths in Ukraine after Zelenskyy warns of Russian strikes
entries.snippet: At least eight people have been killed in air strikes across Ukraine. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned of a "massive Russian attack" citing air force reports, as Kyiv in turn again bombed a logistics center.

entries.title: 'Rienzi': Why this Wagner opera is so relevant today
entries.snippet: The opera sparked controversy long before its Bayreuth Festival premiere, and the debate hasn't died down since it came to the stage. Now, another controversy surrounds the new AI-generated Ring cycle.
